threshold_optimization.method: Cost-sensitive threshold sweep (expected net retention benefit), cross-checked against Youden's J on the ROC curve
threshold_optimization.business_assumptions_reused_from: reports/business_insight_report.md, Section 5 (ARPU annual=$780, CAC=$250, offer cost=$50, campaign success rate=25%)
threshold_optimization.rationale: The default 0.5 threshold is not optimal for this business problem. A pure statistical criterion (Youden's J on the ROC curve) picks threshold=0.5715, but this actually reduces Recall (74.9%) relative to 0.5, which is the wrong direction for churn prevention, where a missed churner (~$1,030 in lost annual revenue + replacement CAC) is far more costly than an unnecessary retention offer (~$50). A theoretical cost-ratio threshold (FP_cost / (FP_cost+FN_cost) = 50/1080 = 0.046) swings too far the other way, flagging ~85% of all customers and making the campaign operationally unfocused. Sweeping thresholds against expected net retention benefit on the held-out test set (using the same ARPU, CAC, offer-cost and campaign-success-rate assumptions as the ROI model in Section 5) peaks around threshold=0.30, which recovers 91.7% of true churners (vs 80.5% at 0.5) at an acceptable Precision (43.4%). This threshold is used as the deployed decision boundary in src/predict.py.
